data.narrative:
Seurat Technologies is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by James DeMuth that has raised $178M to date. The valuation analysis relies on a comparable universe of nine peers—one public (277810.KQ) and eight private firms in the robotics and manufacturing sector at similar or adjacent stages, including Exotec, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Hadrian.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $178M total raised as a proxy for entry valuation and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C to next-stage advancement, implies a valuation of $303M. Peer-median analysis across seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with the peer set ranging from $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer sample includes Exotec at $2.0B (Series D), Hadrian at $1.6B (Series D), Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B (Series B), and Dexterity at $1.6B (Series B).

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $257M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median implied value of $976M. The wide spread reflects material tension between the stage-progression method and peer comparables, likely driven by heterogeneity in peer stage, funding environment at time of raise, and technology maturity. Key uncertainties include the relevance of peer valuations across varied stages and whether Seurat's technology differentiation justifies positioning toward the upper or lower end of the peer range.
